To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the copper-catalyzaed addition of dialkylzincs to N-dipenylphosphinyl imines is a highly enantioselective process if Me-DuPHOs monoxide is used as the chiral ligand.
the addition of diorgnozinc reagents (R2Zn) to imines in the presence of a chiral copper catalyst and a chelating phosphine ligand is an effective method for the preparation of chiral amines.
we discovered a new class of ligands, the BozPHOS ligands, that are capable of catalyzing the addition of organozinc reagents to a broad range of imines with very high enantiocontrol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new chiral phosphine ligands, and the use of these new ligands to catalyze asymmetric reactions.
the design, synthesis, and application of chiral catalysts for asymmetric synthesis.
the development of new synthetic methods for the preparation of chiral compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enantioselective addition of diorgnozinc reagents is a reaction which can be run under a variety of conditions, with a variety of ligands and with a variety of imine substrates.
the enantioselectivity is not due to the formation of a single enantioactive complex.
the enantiocontrol in this catalytic reaction is provided by the copper complex of the Me-DuPHOs monoxide ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a chiral monophosphine ligand can induce a high level of enantioselectivity if the ligand is a monoxide.
the reaction is very efficient and the enantioselectivity is excellent, however the reaction mechanism is still not well understood.
the copper-catalyized asymmetric diorganozinnation of N-diphenlphosphinoyl imines is a robust and reliable method for the synthesis of optically active amines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the copper complex is the active catalyst.
the reaction can be used to prepare a wide range of chiral amines in high yields and enantiomeric excesses.
the reaction is not catalyzed by the chelating Me-DuPHOP ligand itself but rather by a copper complex generated from the ligand and a copper salt.
